chunks: Sa‘d ibn ‘Abdallah narrated from Abu Ja‘far Muhammad ibn ‘Umar ibn Sa‘id, from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub, from Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام, who said:

I heard him saying: I shrouded my father in two Shatawi garments in which he used to enter ihram, and in a shirt from among his shirts, and in a turban that had belonged to ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام, and in a cloak that he had purchased for forty dinars.

key_terms.أَبِي: my father, referring to the Imam's father
key_terms.بُرْدٍ: a cloak or outer garment used in the shrouding
key_terms.ثَوْبَيْنِ: two garments used as part of the shroud
key_terms.دِينَارًا: a gold coin, indicating the garment's purchase value
key_terms.عِمَامَةٍ: a turban belonging to ‘Ali ibn al-Husayn عليهما السلام
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: a shirt included in the burial shrouding
key_terms.كَفَّنْتُ: I prepared the shroud and enshrouded the deceased
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: he would enter the state of ihram using them

ai.seo_question: How did Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام shroud his father according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This report describes how Abu al-Hasan al-Awwal عليه السلام personally shrouded his father using specific garments connected to his life and worship. It preserves a biographical detail about the burial of an Imam and reflects familial care, inherited blessed items, and the use of clothing associated with ihram and dignity.
